the conventional wisdom was that a destabilizing war in the oil-producing heart of the middle east would badly hurt china.
it hasn’t worked out that way. so far, china is weathering the war with iran better than many of its neighbors and looks set to emerge stronger. gzeromedia.com/by-ian-bremme…

netanyahu survived oct. 7 and engineered one of the greatest political comebacks of the era. he hasn't resolved the central tension: what saved him politically may destroy israel's standing internationally. time.com/collection/100-most…

24% of americans think the iran war has been worth the costs and benefits. 35% approve of the military strikes. even among republicans, just 55% say it's been worth it.

nearly half of trump's own party either opposed or uncertain about his signature foreign policy action.

the s&p 500 has fully recovered to pre-iran war levels. the strait of hormuz is still effectively closed, disrupting global supply chains. oil is still near $100. inflation just hit a three-year high. the market has decided none of that matters. ai doing a lot of lifting here.

the us is sending 10,000+ more troops to the middle east while simultaneously pursuing ceasefire talks in islamabad. trump clearly wants to announce a quick win and deescalate. but worth remembering that the pentagon is preparing for "the possibility of additional strikes or ground operations."

trump declaring victory in war with iran and deescalating is by far the smartest move he can make right now. 

would’ve been better weeks ago. but it’s welcome nonetheless.

after winning a free but decidedly unfair election, peter magyar finally allowed on hungarian public television


Magyar Péter (Ne féljetek) (@magyarpeterMP)

As I said, nothing lasts forever. The party-state is falling apart before our eyes. After a year and a half, I will finally appear as a guest on "public" media in a live broadcast tomorrow.

us wholesale inflation hit 4% in march.
gasoline prices up 15.7%, accounting for nearly half the increase. and the march data only captures pricing through march 10th. the full energy shock hasn't shown up in the numbers yet.
(anita no relation to the defeated pm)

post-orban hungary with a decidedly welcome 180 in its approach to foreign policy


Anita Orban (@_OrbanAnita)

The core message is clear: Magyar government will restore freedom, the rule of law, and democratic governance. Not as abstract ideals, but as the foundation of a functioning state.  Hungary aims to rebuild its credibility within NATO and the European Union -  acting as a constructive, reliable partner that contributes to a stronger Europe. the imf's worst case scenario for the iran war:
oil at $110 this year, $125 next year.
inflation hitting 6%.
global growth falling below 2%.
that would be a global recession — the fifth since 1980.

russia taking increased casualties over recent months because of ukrainian drones…now greater than russia’s
troop replacement rate. plus ukraine recently captured a russian position using exclusively drones and unmanned ground vehicles—no soldiers. 

russia’s manpower advantage is now weaker than it has been. hard to see significant territorial gains for the russians in this environment.

the problem is that the reason iran has a stockpile of highly enriched uranium…is because trump unilaterally pulled out of jcpoa. and the reason iran has leverage over the strait…is because trump decided to on a regime change war with iran.

if trump is offering iran renewed jcpoa plus charging tolls for shipping through the strait, that’s a deal they should be willing to accept (the assassination of their supreme leader and political/military leadership notwithstanding).

blockade with ceasefire is a climbdown from last week. second round of talks in islamabad shows president trump looking for an off-ramp. 

iranians happy to continue to engage in negotiations as long as ceasefire continues. more likely to give on nuclear enrichment than influence over the strait…which appears to align with trump’s priorities.

united states and iran closing in on a 12 1/2 year suspension on uranium enrichment…


The New York Times (@nytimes)

Breaking News: In talks, Iran is said to have offered to suspend uranium enrichment for five years; the U.S. is insisting on a 20-year ban.

Follow live updates. nyti.ms/4sxXHo7




— https://nitter.net/nytimes/status/2043822809961361633#m

outstanding and on-the-money thread on what just happened in hungary. worth your moment.


Bogáta Timár (@BogataTimar)

okay I guess I have to talk about Péter Magyar here.
Let me just start with saying, in a very unladylike way, that you guys seem to have zero clue what happened in Hungary in the last two years, you completely miss the point, and you're a disappointing bunch.
Let's go.



— https://nitter.net/BogataTimar/status/2043787197313139178#m

big difference. big implications.
